paper_sentences: In a pre-registered unit-fresh 20% unordered-dyad holdout (311,638 dyad-months; 32,614 positives; 5,282 directed dyads; 2018-01-–2022-11), the frozen temperature-calibrated 49-feature logistic model achieved log-loss 0.21788, Brier 0.06401, ECE 0.04211, AUC 0.9102, and AP 0.6719.

Against the train-only per-dyad Markov baseline (log-loss 0.26587, which equals the global transition on unit-fresh dyads), the primary model reduced log-loss by 0.04800 (18.05% relative; 95% multiway CI [0.04333, 0.05267]; BH q=4.199e-90), increased AUC by 0.17788 and AP by 0.35072, but its ECE was worse by 0.03864 (95% multiway CI [-0.05303, -0.02426]).

Against the stronger warm-history Markov baseline (log-loss 0.20973, ECE 0.01023), the primary model's log-loss was worse by 0.00815 (3.88% relative; 95% multiway CI [-0.01396, -0.00233]) and its ECE was worse by 0.03188 (95% multiway CI [-0.04084, -0.02293]), although its AUC was higher by 0.01598 (95% CI [0.01159, 0.02037]) and AP by 0.03502. The primary model therefore improves ranking but not log-loss or calibration over the best history baseline.

The pre-registered secondary 29-feature logistic model (log-loss 0.20522, ECE 0.02746, AUC 0.9083, AP 0.6717) beat the warm-history Markov baseline on log-loss by 0.00451 (95% multiway CI [0.00142, 0.00760]; p=0.0042; secondary, not in a BH family) but not on ECE (-0.01724; 95% CI [-0.02298, -0.01149]); the 20 graph features in the primary do not help on this holdout.

A 29-feature year-fixed-effects anchor achieved log-loss 0.20063, ECE 0.02037, AUC 0.9084, and AP 0.6724, better than the primary on log-loss; calendar specification, not graph capacity, drives the holdout differences.

Within-dyad AUC was 0.5266 (P1-compatible) and 0.5616 (strict pair-weighted; mean 0.5139) for the primary model, versus 0.5315 (P1-compatible) for per-dyad Markov; the dyad fixed-effects/conditional-logit check gave 0.5597 strict (P1-compatible 0.5561). The fixed-effects check shows some within-dyad signal; any month-level timing claim is exploratory.
The confirmatory claim is limited to dyad-level event propensity/ranking plus an exploratory within-dyad timing signal; we make no node-level prediction claim and no causal/lifecycle claim.

Because the holdout is unit-fresh rather than time-fresh and the 2018-22 period was retrospectively burned by earlier runs, these results are retrospective and should not be presented as a prospective forecast.
